forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./31/children: These families appear repeatedly, but the exact names, schedules, populations and units differ across countries. The table is a vocabulary guide, not a ranking that tells you which release will move prices most. Use the original agency or survey provider’s definitions, and separate an official statistic from a private forecast.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./32/children: For many PMI activity indexes, a reading above 50 indicates more respondents reporting improvement than deterioration under that index’s methodology. A value of 55 is not GDP growth of 55% or a 55% chance of a currency rise. Components can have different interpretations, such as supplier-delivery measures, so read the specific series rather than applying one rule to every row.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./33/children: A calendar’s forecast may be a survey median, average or another provider estimate. It is not every participant’s belief or a direct measurement of all expectations priced into markets. Save its source and timestamp before the release. If you only copy a forecast after publication, you may accidentally use a revised number or an estimate that was never available beforehand.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./34/children/0: An invented report forecasts 220,000 payroll jobs and records 190,000. The level is positive, but the difference from this forecast is −30,000. In another example, an expected 150,000 versus actual 190,000 gives +40,000. The same actual can have a different surprise relative to different saved expectations.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./35/rows/0/1: How did this estimate differ from the prior estimate?
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./35/rows/1/1: What changed from the measured earlier period?
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./35/rows/2/1: What was corrected in earlier information?
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./36/children: A forecast miss and a currency move occurring together do not prove that the release alone caused every change. Another country’s news, revised components, positioning and liquidity can act at the same time. Describe possible channels and alternatives; avoid replacing uncertainty with a dramatic headline.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./37/children: A release date is not the same as the period the statistic describes. A jobs report published this month may describe last month. A GDP estimate may cover a completed quarter, and an annual inflation rate compares a year-long interval ending earlier. Prices around publication react to newly available information and expectations, not necessarily to an economic change beginning at that second.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./38/title: A report card describes earlier work
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./38/children/0: A learner in South Korea receives a school report in October about work completed earlier. The publication is new information, while the studied period is older. A market release has the same separation between measurement period and publication time.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./39/children: Record four dates where relevant: measurement period, scheduled publication, actual publication and your observation timestamp. This matters if a release is delayed, corrected or revised. Using a later revised series to explain an earlier decision can introduce future information, just as using an unconfirmed swing did in Level 6.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./40/children: The first move can reverse after readers examine components or a policy explanation. You do not need to invent one reason that explains the whole path. A notebook can say “headline initially appeared above the saved forecast; spread widened; later prices reversed; other causes remain possible.”
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./41/children: Fundamental analysis proposes explanations; the risk worksheet asks what a stated position could cost. Neither should silently replace the other. If you already have a demo position, inspect common currency exposure and release-related execution assumptions. If you are observing without a position, a hypothetical price calculation can teach units without becoming a forecast.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./42/description: For supported EUR/USD, use a USD account, conversion 1, 0.01 lot, long entry 1.1000 and hypothetical exit 1.0950. The price-only result is −US$5. This scenario does not say that any release will cause that move; add charges and worse-fill assumptions separately.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./43/children: A Brazil importer’s USD/BRL bill uses a different pair and purpose from that supported tool exercise. Do not force an unsupported instrument into a calculator or treat a spot payment as identical to a leveraged derivative. Always name the product and quote convention. A strong economic story does not remove minimum-size, margin, cost or loss-limit checks.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./44/children/0: No headline, calendar icon or economic model guarantees an exchange-rate direction, a fill or a maximum loss. Keep essential living money outside trading experiments and use observation or demo while definitions and assumptions are unclear.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./45/prompt: An importer owes US$100. What are the before-fee bills at invented USD/BRL 5.00 and 5.20? What is the increase as a percentage of the first bill?
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./46/children: R$500 and R$520. The increase is R$20/500 = 4%. This is payment arithmetic, not a forecast or proof of which news caused the rate change.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./47/prompt: An invented price index rises from 100 to 104, then 106. Does slowing inflation mean the second price level fell?
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./48/children: No. The changes are 4% and about 1.92%. Prices rose more slowly; the level is still higher. State the period and series before calling a number an inflation rate.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./49/prompt: An actual payroll estimate is 190,000 versus a saved 150,000 forecast, while the prior figure is revised down by 60,000. What should the record include?
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./50/children: Headline surprise +40,000 and the separate −60,000 prior revision, plus other components and the saved forecast source/time. Do not turn their simple sum into a guaranteed currency signal.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./51/prompt: A quarterly real GDP change is reported as 1% nonannualised. If repeated for four quarters, approximately what annualised rate corresponds to that arithmetic?
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./52/children: (1.01^4 − 1) × 100 ≈ 4.06%. This annualisation is a convention based on repetition, not four observed quarters or a future growth promise.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./53/title: Explain it in your own words
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./53/points/0: Explain currency demand through payments, investment and changing expectations.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./53/points/1: Read inflation, employment and growth with the correct units and revisions.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./53/points/2: Separate an actual/forecast comparison from a guaranteed currency response.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./53/closing/0: Keep the source, units, observation time and saved expectations in your notebook. Describe possible explanations without presenting them as certain causes or trading signals.
forex:economic-news-and-currency-demand./54/children: All numerical examples are invented teaching scenarios, not forecasts or trade recommendations. News, policy, calendars and relationships cannot guarantee price direction, execution or a maximum loss. Leverage, costs, conversion, gaps and product terms matter. Keep essential living money outside trading experiments.

forex:emotions-around-a-decision./0/children: Trading psychology concerns how feelings, attention and habits can affect decisions made under uncertainty. A feeling is real, but it is not a quote, a completed candle or proof of what the market will do next. Fear, excitement, frustration and boredom can all appear during a learning session. You do not need to feel nothing to make a careful decision.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./1/children: The task in this lesson is to separate what you noticed, what you felt, what the written rule permitted and what you actually did. The examples use invented prices and demo exercises. A pause, an observation without an order and a decision to stop studying for the day can all be complete decisions. There is no requirement to trade in order to finish the lesson.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./2/children/0: A shopper in the United Kingdom enters a supermarket hungry and wants extra snacks. The hunger is real, but it does not change the shopping budget. Checking the list before paying makes the decision easier to review. A trading learner can likewise acknowledge an urge without using it to rewrite a price condition or cash limit.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./3/children: Psychology cannot turn a weak method into a reliable one, repair a faulty data feed or make an ordinary stop guarantee its price. Earlier lessons on product terms, execution, shared exposure and cash risk still apply. Good records help you see which kind of problem occurred instead of blaming every loss on your feelings.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./4/children: Fear can appear before an action, while a position is open or after an adverse outcome. A learner might avoid a planned demo observation, close a position for an unwritten reason or repeatedly move between timeframes looking for reassurance. Record the action and the rule comparison, rather than attaching a permanent label such as “I am a fearful trader” to yourself.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./5/children: Sometimes hesitation points to a real missing input. You may not understand the contract, account conversion, stop trigger or news schedule. Pausing to clarify that information is sensible. Do not force yourself to continue just to demonstrate courage. Ask whether a required condition is unknown, an account gate failed or the urge conflicts with a clear, previously written condition.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./6/children/0: A learner in Japan approaches an unfamiliar junction. Stopping to read the signs is useful; driving through to prove confidence is not. In a demo platform, an unclear order type deserves the same pause. Fear is not evidence that the order is wrong, and confidence is not evidence that it is right.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./7/rows/0/0: The product or quote side is unclear
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./7/rows/0/1: Clarify it; keep the action unclassified or skip
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./7/rows/1/0: A written exposure gate has failed
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./7/rows/1/1: Follow the gate and its existing-order procedure
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./7/rows/2/0: All required information is recorded, but an urge conflicts with the plan
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./7/rows/2/1: Record the urge and use the prewritten pause/review procedure
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./7/rows/3/1: Stop new practice actions and schedule a separate review
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./7/rows/4/1: End or reduce the study session; no order is required
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./8/children: Greed is a useful everyday word for wanting more than the plan allows. In a journal, replace the vague label with a specific action: size increased without approval, a target moved after a paper gain, another correlated position added or a risk gate ignored. Excitement after a win can produce similar changes. The action is what you can check later.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./9/title: A sale does not enlarge the budget
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./9/children/0: A Canadian family sees a discount and adds items it had not planned to buy. Each item may look attractive, yet the total bill can exceed the budget. Several apparently attractive demo positions can likewise exceed the account’s combined exposure even if each individual chart looks convincing.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./10/children: A rising account balance does not automatically authorise a larger size. The reference balance, percentage, maximum combined exposure and conditions for recalculation belong in the prewritten policy. If a plan permits some management change, state its trigger and limits beforehand. A permitted change and an impulsive change may look similar on a final screenshot but have different decision histories.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./11/children: A profit screenshot can create the impression that more risk was justified. Keep the plan version and the time when the change was made. A winning rule breach remains a breach; it does not become evidence that the original cash limit was unnecessary. Review the decision without celebrating or condemning the person.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./12/children: Overtrading means taking actions that exceed what the stated method, risk policy or practical schedule supports. There is no universal number of trades that separates careful practice from overtrading. One unplanned trade can be too many; several planned observation entries can belong to a structured exercise. Count what the rule permits and what actually happened.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./13/children: Look for repeated entries without a fresh qualifying condition, switching pairs merely to find activity, continuing past a session cutoff or treating boredom as a signal. Opening and closing again can add spread and fees without adding a valid observation. Reopening after an exit may be a different candidate and needs an explicit re-entry rule, not the assumption that the previous idea remains active forever.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./14/children/0: An Italian gardener checks a plant, feels impatient and waters it repeatedly even when the soil is already wet. More actions are not automatically better care. A learner staring at a quiet chart may also create unnecessary actions simply to feel busy.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./16/children: The extra eight round trips add US$4.00 in this deliberately simple fixed-charge example. Real charges vary by size, product and provider, and spreads or financing may add more. This table does not establish a profitable trade count; it shows why extra activity deserves a cost record.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./17/children: Revenge trading is a rushed attempt to recover a loss through a new action rather than a fresh, qualifying decision. Common signs include “I need it back today,” doubling size after each loss, entering another pair without analysis or extending the session until the balance returns to a preferred number. The previous loss does not create a market obligation to repay you.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./18/title: The board game does not owe a win
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./18/children/0: A child in France loses a board game and proposes double stakes for the next round. The larger stake changes the possible loss; it does not improve the dice. Real Forex outcomes are more complex and need not be independent, but an earlier loss still cannot by itself prove that a later win is due.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./19/caption: Invented escalation of planned cash risk, assuming exact full-risk losses
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./19/columns/2: Cumulative stated loss if each loses
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./20/children: The four stated losses total US$150. A next doubling would put US$160 at risk before costs and any worse execution. This is not a recovery method or recommendation. It demonstrates how an emotional response can change the loss scale faster than the learner notices. Actual loss can differ from the planned amount because of fills, costs and product conditions.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./21/children/0: Do not borrow essential household money, add funds or raise leverage merely to erase an uncomfortable result. Record the completed loss and follow the written pause and exposure procedure. An earlier loss is a fact to account for, not a reason to abandon limits.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./22/children: Fear of missing out, often shortened to FOMO, can appear when a price moves quickly or another person posts a profitable-looking screenshot. The urge says “act now.” Your rule asks whether the allowed price, time window, chart condition and account gates are still satisfied. Urgency cannot answer those questions.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./23/children/0: A commuter in Australia misses a bus. Running into traffic would introduce a new risk rather than complete the original safe journey. Missing a chart move similarly does not create a duty to chase it. Another observation session can occur without recovering the missed move.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./24/children: In the AUD/USD teaching example, a learner’s demo rule permits an entry only below an invented ask of 0.6600 within its defined window. The current ask is 0.6640. The permitted price condition is false. An entry at exactly 0.6600 would also fail the strictly-below condition; a rule allowing equality would be a different rule.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./25/children: Record “missed, no entry,” the feeling and the unavailable condition. If price later rises, keep the same classification. If it later falls, do not claim that the skip was a prediction. The process was a check of the rule at the decision time. A new candidate needs a new qualifying condition under the declared method.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./26/alt: A process flow separates noticing an urge, checking the written rule and recording a permitted action or a skip.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./26/caption: This is an observation/demo decision aid, not a validated emotion test or a promise of profit. Unclear conditions remain unresolved.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./27/children: A late entry changes more than the entry label. With an unchanged stop, it can increase adverse distance, reduce the original target distance or leave a target on the wrong side of the entry. A calculator can make that change visible, but cannot grant permission to break the price rule. Check rule eligibility first and keep an ineligible scenario as a paper comparison only.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./28/caption: Invented AUD/USD long comparison, one conventional pip = 0.0001
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./29/children: The original entry 0.6595 is below 0.6600; the late entry is not. At a conventional 100,000 AUD per standard lot, 0.01 lot is 1,000 AUD. The paper price losses are 1,000 × 0.0020 = US$2.00 and 1,000 × 0.0065 = US$6.50. Both omit charges and any worse fill. The old target is not a favourable long target from 0.6640.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./30/description: Use supported AUD/USD, a USD account, conversion 1 and 0.01 lot. Compare long entry 0.6595/exit 0.6575 with long entry 0.6640/exit 0.6575. The price results are −US$2 and −US$6.50 under the tool’s contract assumptions. This paper comparison does not authorise the late entry.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./31/children: Reducing the late scenario’s size would not repair the failed entry condition. Chart eligibility, product execution and cash risk are separate gates. If a proposed new rule permits late entries, review it later as a new version rather than silently inserting it into the old plan after seeing the move.

forex:emotions-around-a-decision./32/rows/6/1: Did I preserve the original rule and evidence?
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./33/children: Use ordinary words for feelings. You do not need a medical diagnosis or a score to write “frustrated, wanted to chase.” If you use a personal one-to-five intensity scale, define it consistently and treat it as a notebook aid, not a clinical assessment or a universal trading threshold. The score cannot replace product or account checks.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./34/title: A receipt and a reaction are different records
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./34/children/0: A shopper in Germany writes the receipt total, then notes disappointment that it was higher than expected. The receipt is not changed by the feeling. A journal can hold facts and feelings together without letting one replace the other.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./35/children: Write the action that actually occurred, even when it differs from the plan. “Wanted to chase but placed no order” differs from “submitted an order then cancelled it.” A cancellation request can fail or arrive after activation, so record platform confirmation and the current order/position list rather than only the intention.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./36/children: A pause procedure names the trigger, action and conditions for review or resumption. “Calm down” is too vague to check. A teaching example might say: when I notice an urge to change an entry or size outside the plan, I stop new demo submissions, save the quote and rule comparison, and review the written gates before deciding whether the session ends.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./37/children: A pause is not automatically a fixed number of minutes. The appropriate action depends on the purpose, existing exposure and practical circumstances. Waiting briefly does not make an ineligible price eligible, undo a reached loss gate or resolve missing contract information. Set any time rule beforehand and avoid describing it as a universal safe interval.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./38/rows/0/1: What observable urge, breach or unresolved condition occurred?
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./38/rows/1/1: Are new demo submissions paused under this policy?
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./38/rows/2/1: Which positions/pending orders still require the specified handling?
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./38/rows/3/1: What quote, rule version, timestamp and platform confirmation are saved?
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./38/rows/4/1: Which information or account gates must be checked?
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./38/rows/5/1: What written conditions allow resumption, or end the session?
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./39/children: Do not assume that a pause button means all exposure disappeared. Closing, cancelling or modifying orders involves product rules and execution risks. Follow the existing written procedure, verify the resulting state and avoid improvised changes driven by the same urge that triggered the pause. Observation-only practice can simply end without an order.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./40/children: Build a study environment that supports the task you actually chose. Close unrelated profit feeds, turn off nonessential alerts, prepare the notebook and select one observation question before opening charts. These are practical design choices, not guarantees of emotional control or trading success. A distraction-free session still needs a valid method and accurate inputs.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./41/title: The phone stays away from the homework
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./41/children/0: A student in India puts social notifications aside while solving one maths exercise. That makes it easier to follow the question but does not make an incorrect formula correct. A learner reviewing EUR/USD can similarly remove distractions while still checking the rule and units.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./42/children: A screenshot from a group chat may omit size, leverage, losses, fees, timestamps or whether the balance is simulated. Treat it as incomplete information rather than a benchmark you must match. A person’s confident language is not proof of an applicable method. Verify sources and product facts separately from how an advertisement makes you feel.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./43/children: Choose a realistic end time and protect ordinary commitments. If the exercise is repeatedly interrupted, shorten it or choose a different task. A reliable ten-minute observation may teach more than a long session of unrecorded entries. Keep personal logins, balance details and identifying information private when asking another learner to review a record.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./44/children: After an impulse action, first establish what actually happened: order status, open/pending exposure, fill prices and charges. Apply the existing handling policy rather than an improvised attempt to recover. Then record the decision sequence. Explain the trigger, missing check or rule breach specifically; “bad mindset” does not tell you what to change.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./45/title: One burnt loaf is useful evidence
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./45/children/0: A baker in Italy burns a loaf and checks oven temperature, timing and the recipe. The loaf does not prove that the baker is a failure. A demo error can likewise become a concrete review: the learner submitted before checking the price ceiling, so the next practice session includes reading that line aloud.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./46/children: A useful corrective action is observable: keep the entry ceiling visible, require the account worksheet before submission or stop new practice when the stated gate triggers. Change one practical step and review its effect on later records. Do not promise that naming the feeling will eliminate all future errors. If the method itself is unclear, work on its definition before collecting more trades.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./47/children: When money pressure, stress or screen time interferes with daily responsibilities, pause or reduce the activity and seek appropriate support from trusted people or qualified services. This course is educational, not mental-health treatment. You can decide that active trading does not belong in your life; completing the course does not require a deposit or live account.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./48/prompt: Your rule requires AUD/USD ask strictly below 0.6600. The ask is 0.6640 and a friend says the move will continue. What belongs in the journal?
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./49/children: The price condition is false: missed, no entry. Record the quote/time, original rule, feeling and urge separately. A friend’s forecast or later rally does not rewrite the condition.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./50/prompt: At 0.01 lot, compare the paper long loss from 0.6595 to 0.6575 with the loss from 0.6640 to 0.6575 in a USD account.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./51/children: 20 pips versus 65 pips, or US$2 versus US$6.50 before charges under a 100,000-unit contract. The later scenario remains ineligible under the original entry rule.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./52/prompt: Four exact hypothetical losses use planned amounts US$10, US$20, US$40 and US$80. What is the total, and does it make a later win due?
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./53/children: The total is US$150 before additional costs or worse fills. Previous losses alone do not establish the next outcome or justify escalation.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./54/prompt: You pause new orders but a pending demo order remains. Has the pause automatically removed exposure?
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./55/children: No. The order may still activate. Follow the written product-specific procedure, check confirmations and the current order/position list, and record what actually happened.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./56/title: Explain it in your own words
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./56/points/0: Separate market facts, feelings, urges and actual actions in a dated record.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./56/points/1: Identify chasing, excessive activity and recovery-driven size escalation.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./56/points/2: Use a checkable pause procedure and compare late-entry cash scenarios without changing the rule.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./56/closing/0: Keep the original plan and information cutoff. Record feelings, actions, process quality and later outcomes separately, including skips and uncertainties.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./57/children: All prices, balances, thresholds and schedules are invented teaching examples, not trade recommendations or universal safe limits. Psychology knowledge, routines and rule-following do not guarantee profit, exact fills or a maximum loss. Leverage, costs, conversion, gaps and product terms matter. Keep essential money outside trading experiments. This course is educational, not mental-health treatment.

forex:emotions-around-a-decision./58/points/0: I can distinguish a fact, a feeling, an urge and an action.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./58/points/1: I can compare the decision with the saved rule without using the later outcome.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./58/points/2: I can keep all relevant records, costs, skips and uncertainties visible.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./58/points/3: I can explain a valid pause or no-action reason.
forex:emotions-around-a-decision./58/points/4: I can use the highlighted tools as arithmetic checks and state their limitations.

forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./0/children: Position value, required margin and account equity answer different questions. Position value describes exposure. Required margin is the provider’s current collateral requirement. Equity describes the account value including open results under the provider’s rules. Confusing them can make a large position look small simply because it needed a small deposit.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./1/title: The deposit is not the full responsibility
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./1/children/0: An Australian learner hires equipment worth A$2,000 and pays an A$200 deposit. The deposit is not the equipment’s value or a promise that every possible bill is capped at A$200. This is only an everyday analogy: leveraged trading is governed by its own product and account terms. It helps separate collateral from exposure.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./2/children: Leverage means obtaining exposure larger than the money supporting it. Depending on the product, this may involve borrowing, financing or a derivative position rather than a literal loan paid into your bank account. There is no single founder of the broad idea of leverage or margin; they are financing and collateral concepts used across different markets. This lesson teaches their arithmetic, while the exact legal arrangement must come from the provider’s documents.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./3/children: In a conventional linear EUR/USD example, 0.10 lot represents 10,000 euros. At 1.1000 USD per euro, that is US$11,000 of notional exposure. Notional means the face-value reference for the position; it is not the cash profit, the stop risk or necessarily the cash paid to enter. Its account-currency equivalent changes with the chosen conversion rate.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./4/expression: Illustrative account-currency notional = base units × pair price × quote-to-account conversion
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./4/explanation: Use the actual contract multiplier and the units of each conversion. This simplified linear model is not universal across products.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./5/children/0: 10,000 EUR × 1.1000 USD per EUR = US$11,000. In a USD account the additional quote-to-account conversion is 1. If the price falls from 1.1000 to 1.0990, the long’s price result is 10,000 × (−0.0010) = −US$10 before charges, whatever margin was required.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./6/children: For a short, the sign reverses: a rise is adverse and a fall favourable before costs. Check the instrument’s specifications rather than assuming every platform symbol is spot Forex. A futures contract, CFD or another derivative can have different multipliers, margin methods and settlement. Use one declared product throughout the example.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./7/children: A stated leverage allowance such as 20:1 describes an illustrative relationship between notional and required margin. Under a simple fixed-rate model, required margin is notional divided by that leverage. The corresponding margin rate is 100 divided by leverage, expressed as a percentage. A provider can use tiers, separate long/short rules, different instruments or changed requirements, so the platform’s actual rule takes priority.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./8/caption: Same US$11,000 exposure under invented fixed margin rates
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./9/children: The table keeps the position size and price move fixed. Changing the margin allowance changes the collateral requirement; it does not change that position’s US$10 price loss. If someone uses the released collateral to open a larger position, the cash exposure then increases because size changed. Keep those two situations separate.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./10/description: Use EUR/USD, 0.10 lot, price 1.1000, USD account and conversion 1. Compare leverage inputs 10, 20 and 50. Expected simplified margins are US$1,100, US$550 and US$220. The tool does not model provider-specific tiers or liquidation.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./11/children: Allowed leverage and used leverage are different. Effective account leverage compares the notional exposure actually held with account equity. In a multi-position worksheet, state whether you are summing gross absolute exposures or using a net convention. Gross exposure helps reveal large offsetting tickets that a net figure can hide. Neither number alone describes every risk.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./12/expression: Illustrative effective leverage = gross account-currency notional ÷ current equity
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./12/explanation: A simplified exposure ratio. Use consistent conversion and account valuation; gross and net conventions must be labelled.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./13/children/0: A$1,000 of equity supports an invented A$2,000 currency exposure requiring A$200 margin. Effective exposure is 2:1, even though exposure relative to this margin is 10:1. In a simplified 5% adverse move measured on that account-currency exposure, the price loss is A$100, or 10% of the initial account equity—not 5% of the A$200 margin.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./14/children: When equity falls while the position remains open, effective leverage can rise without adding a ticket. If equity fell to A$800 and exposure remained approximately A$2,000, the ratio would be 2.5:1. Exchange-rate conversion can also change the numerator. This is why a leverage allowance is not a risk budget and a displayed maximum is not a target to use.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./15/children: To isolate the arithmetic, assume a linear account-currency exposure equal to equity multiplied by an effective leverage ratio. Then a 1% adverse exposure move produces a loss equal to that ratio times 1% of starting equity, before costs and close-out effects. These examples deliberately hold other inputs constant; they do not assert how often a currency moves 1% or that a provider would allow every position to remain open.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./16/caption: Invented US$1,000 account; 1% adverse move before costs
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./17/children: A favourable move has the opposite price effect under the same simplified assumptions. Leverage amplifies both directions; it does not improve the forecast. At very high exposure, a comparatively small adverse move can consume the equity or trigger close-out before the worksheet’s final price. Losses can exceed the deposit for some products and jurisdictions; protections must be verified, not assumed.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./18/children/0: Do not describe margin as the amount you are willing to lose. Do not infer that a small price move creates a small cash loss. Calculate the full position’s sensitivity and examine account terms before comparing percentages.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./19/children: A common simple account display uses free margin equal to equity minus used margin, and margin level equal to equity divided by used margin times 100. Actual credit, blocked-profit and margin rules can add details. Free margin is a capacity calculation under those rules; it is not money that is automatically safe to risk. An open position can continue losing while the number is positive.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./20/caption: Invented USD account; used margin held at US$550
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./21/children: This table is an arithmetic snapshot, not a promised sequence of permitted trades. The provider might intervene earlier, and used margin might change with prices, rules or exposure. When used margin is zero, the equity-to-margin percentage is undefined; a blank or special display must not be interpreted as a numeric guarantee.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./22/children/0: A Japanese household can see the same bank deposit while expected expenses rise. The amount available for a new commitment falls. On a trading account, open results and margin requirements can both change, so a balance screenshot alone cannot show the current capacity or risk.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./23/children: A margin-call condition means the account has reached the provider’s warning or requirement threshold. A stop-out or liquidation condition allows or requires forced closure under its rules. There may be no phone call and no period to wait for a recovery. Some systems block new orders; others close positions in a specified order. Thresholds may be percentages or amounts. Read the contract, not another learner’s platform screenshot.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./24/children/0: Suppose an invented policy warns at a 100% margin level and starts forced closure at 50%. With used margin held at US$550, the warning equity is US$550 and the 50% threshold is US$275. These numbers are not PipStart recommendations or a statement of any broker’s real policy.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./24/children/1: A fast move might pass the threshold before an orderly fill is available. Used margin can change as positions close. Therefore this simple calculation identifies a condition in an assumed model, not an exact liquidation price or final account loss.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./25/children: Adding funds does not make an unsound position sound. If a demo worksheet relies on transferring household money to keep a losing position open, stop and review the policy rather than treating the transfer as risk control. Essential money stays outside the experiment. Confirm whether negative-balance protection applies to your entity, client classification and product; it cannot be inferred from a familiar brand name.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./26/children: Before any live consideration, independently verify the provider and its account terms, margin-change rights, order triggers, close-out method and complaint process. A profitable-looking chart cannot answer those contract questions. The broker lessons remain relevant here.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./27/children: A margin requirement can increase while price has not moved against the position. If US$11,000 exposure initially needs US$220 at a 2% rate, a hypothetical change to 5% needs US$550. With US$1,000 equity, free margin falls from US$780 to US$450 under the simple equation. An unchanged account balance does not mean unchanged capacity.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./28/children: News, session transitions, gaps, poor liquidity, technology problems and provider policy can affect execution. A personal stop may be triggered and filled after an adverse move; an account-level forced closure can occur independently of your intended chart invalidation. Even a position whose intended stop risk looked small can be unsuitable if margin capacity and execution assumptions are fragile.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./29/children/0: A traveller in Germany reserves a rental with a €100 deposit. If the contract allows the deposit to rise to €250, the planned spending capacity changes even if the rental has not been damaged. The lesson is to read the requirement and keep room for changes, not to assume trading contracts operate exactly like rentals.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./30/children: In demo, document separate checks: planned stop loss, adverse-fill loss, current margin, a higher-margin scenario, and combined positions. Do not use the Margin Calculator’s simple result as proof that a provider will accept the order or that forced closure will happen at the same number.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./31/children: Drawdown is the fall from a previous account high to a later value. Choose a consistent series: balance-only drawdown omits open losses, while equity drawdown captures the account valuation including them. Record both where available rather than presenting the smaller one as the whole story. Maximum drawdown over a period is the largest recorded peak-to-subsequent-trough decline, not the sum of every losing trade.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./32/expression: Drawdown % = (previous peak − later account value) ÷ previous peak × 100
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./32/explanation: Use the same account-value convention and adjust the record for deposits/withdrawals when assessing performance.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./33/title: A peak, a fall, then a partial recovery
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./33/children/0: An invented account moves from US$1,000 to US$1,200, falls to US$960, then rises to US$1,080. The drawdown at US$960 is US$240/US$1,200 = 20%. At US$1,080 it is 10% below the same peak. The peak does not reset to US$960 merely because that is convenient.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./34/children: Fresh deposits can hide trading losses if you look only at the ending balance; withdrawals can look like losses when they are not. Separate external cash flows from trading results. An intraday trough may be deeper than an end-of-day record captures, so state the observation frequency as well as the account convention.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./35/children: A loss percentage uses the old amount as its denominator. Recovery uses the smaller amount remaining. A 20% fall from 100 to 80 loses 20, but gaining those 20 back requires 20/80 = 25%. This arithmetic explains why “I will just gain the same percentage back” is wrong. It does not promise a recovery path.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./36/explanation: Valid for a decline below 100%. At a 100% loss there is no remaining capital from which to grow.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./37/caption: Loss and recovery on a US$1,000 teaching account
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./38/alt: A teaching account falls from 100 to 80: loss is 20% of 100; regaining 20 is 25% of 80.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./38/caption: The amount needed is the same 20; the denominator changes. Recovery is arithmetic, not a target the market owes you.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./39/title: A water tank makes the denominator visible
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./39/children/0: A household in South Africa has 100 litres in a tank and uses 20. The 80 litres remaining need 20 added, which is one quarter of 80. The tank example uses the same arithmetic as the account, without suggesting that money can be replenished as predictably as water.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./40/description: Enter a hypothetical USD account of 1,000 and a 20% decline. Compare US$800 remaining and 25% recovery required. The tool does not predict when or whether recovery occurs.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./41/children: A recovery calculation describes the distance back to an earlier value. It does not justify increasing leverage, doubling size or taking a new idea to erase a loss quickly. A new trade must pass the same independent rules as the first one. Time spent learning can be more useful than taking another position; a loss is not a deadline to earn it back.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./42/description: Use current demo value 800 and recovery target 1,000. A constant 5% gain per period would require five whole periods in the model. That assumed growth rate is not a forecast, income promise or appropriate objective.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./43/children: The constant-growth model compounds a chosen rate. Four 5% periods give about 972.41 from 800; five give about 1,021.03. Real trading can alternate gains and losses, costs and withdrawals; a fixed growth path conceals that uncertainty. Label the assumption clearly and do not convert the calculator’s output into a date by which the account must recover.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./44/children/0: A smaller remaining balance, a larger recovery percentage and emotional pressure can combine badly. Pause, review total exposure and check whether the original learning activity still fits your circumstances. No course completion, calculator or broker allowance makes essential money available for risk.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./45/prompt: A EUR/USD teaching position is 0.10 lot, or 10,000 euros, at 1.1000. In a USD account and a simple 20:1 margin model, find notional and required margin. What is a 10-pip adverse price loss?
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./46/children: Notional is US$11,000 and margin is US$550. The price loss is US$10 before costs. Margin does not cap that loss, and provider rules may differ from the fixed-rate model.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./47/prompt: A demo balance is US$1,000, floating result −US$100 and used margin US$550. Assume no other adjustments. Find equity, free margin and margin level.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./48/children: Equity is US$900; free margin US$350; margin level 900/550 × 100 = about 163.64%. The positive free margin is not a statement that another trade is safe.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./49/prompt: An account peaks at US$1,200 and later reaches US$960. Find drawdown and the gain needed to regain the peak.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./50/children: Drawdown is 20%. Recovery requires US$240/US$960 = 25%, before costs and external cash flows. These are different denominators.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./51/title: Explain it in your own words
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./51/points/0: Distinguish notional exposure, required margin and effective account leverage.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./51/points/1: Calculate equity, free margin and hypothetical margin-level conditions.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./51/points/2: Measure drawdown and recovery with consistent account references.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./51/closing/0: Use a demo notebook to keep intended risk, actual outcomes and unexplained differences separate. If you cannot explain a unit or assumption, pause and check it.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./52/children: All numeric market and account examples are invented teaching data, not live recommendations. Position sizing, stops and loss limits cannot guarantee a maximum actual loss. Product terms, leverage, conversion, charges, gaps and execution can change results. Keep essential living money outside trading experiments.

forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./53/points/1: I can distinguish account values, planned losses and actual outcomes.
forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./53/points/2: I can identify a cost or execution assumption that could fail.

forex:margin-leverage-and-drawdown./53/points/4: I can state when a zero-size decision or a learning pause is appropriate.

forex:policy-and-market-relationships./0/children: Policy and market relationships help explain how economic decisions might reach currencies. They are not a shortcut from a headline to a buy or sell instruction. Begin with three separate questions: what was decided, how it differed from the expectations recorded beforehand, and which possible channels could matter. The outcome depends on other countries, market positioning, liquidity and later information as well.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./1/title: The announced fee was already expected
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./1/children/0: A school in the United Kingdom announces a £5 increase in its monthly activity fee. If parents expected £5, the announcement confirms their plan. If they expected £10, the same increase is smaller than expected. A policy-rate increase can likewise be an increase in level without being a positive surprise relative to a saved expectation.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./2/children: The framework here builds on the previous lesson’s units, revisions and comparison rules. Use invented examples to practise explanation and alternative outcomes. Avoid writing “higher rates mean the currency must rise.” A conditional explanation is stronger when it names the information that could weaken it.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./3/children: Monetary policy is conducted through a country’s central-bank framework and can involve policy interest rates, lending facilities and balance-sheet operations. Fiscal policy involves government spending, taxation and borrowing. Their authorities, legal mandates and operating arrangements differ across countries. A government budget is not the same announcement as a central-bank rate decision.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./4/rows/0/1: Central bank changes its policy rate
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./4/rows/0/2: What changed, what was expected, and what does the explanation imply?
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./4/rows/1/2: When does it take effect, who is affected, and how is it financed?
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./4/rows/2/1: Spending supports demand while rates restrict borrowing
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./4/rows/2/2: What might happen to demand, inflation, financing and confidence?
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./5/title: The family budget and the bank loan
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./5/children/0: A Canadian household changes its spending plan while its bank changes the rate on a loan. These affect the same household through different decisions. Government spending and central-bank rates can also affect the same economy through different channels. The analogy helps separate the decisions; a country’s institutions and economy are much more complex.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./6/children: Expansionary and restrictive are useful descriptions of intended effects, not certain outcomes. More spending may support demand but also raise financing or inflation concerns. Higher rates may slow borrowing but their effect takes time and varies by household and business. Check the actual measures rather than judging an entire package from one label.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./7/children: Quantitative easing, or QE, involves central-bank asset purchases financed through newly created central-bank reserves under the relevant programme. It aims to influence financial conditions, including borrowing costs. Quantitative tightening, or QT, unwinds purchased assets, for example through maturities without full reinvestment or through sales. Programme details matter; these are not simply a cash gift to every household or a guaranteed currency direction. The Bank of England began its UK QE programme in March 2009 during the financial crisis. That is the beginning of that programme, not the origin of all central banking.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./8/children: Central banks have different mandates, instruments and institutional arrangements. Price stability is a common concern, but employment, financial stability and other responsibilities vary. Some exchange-rate regimes also constrain the choices available. Do not assume that the Federal Reserve, Bank of England, European Central Bank and another central bank all operate under identical objectives.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./9/children: There is no single founder of modern fundamental analysis or one origin date for all central banking. Institutions and analytical approaches developed over time. For a beginner, the important historical distinction is that today’s policies belong to specific legal institutions and evolving monetary arrangements. Learn the named institution’s own explanation before applying a general label.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./10/children/0: A worker in Germany and a worker in Japan may both receive safety instructions, but the rules at their employers are not identical. Likewise, two central banks can both discuss inflation while using different mandates and decision procedures. Read the institution’s own documents.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./11/columns/1: Why it belongs in the notebook
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./11/rows/0/1: Central bank, treasury, statistics agency or another body
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./11/rows/1/1: Official objectives and relevant legal framework
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./11/rows/3/1: Statement, projections, minutes or press conference
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./11/rows/5/1: An interpretation is not a guaranteed price response
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./12/children: A policy rate is a current setting. Market participants also consider the possible path of later settings. A decision that leaves today’s rate unchanged may still accompany an explanation that changes expectations about future decisions. Forward guidance communicates policy intentions or conditions, but it is not an unconditional promise that every later decision will follow a fixed timetable.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./13/title: A bus is on time but the later service changes
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./13/children/0: An Australian commuter sees that the current bus leaves on time. A notice says later services may be less frequent if road work continues. Today’s departure and the future schedule are different pieces of information. A rate decision and its accompanying guidance also deserve separate entries.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./14/rows/2/2: Statement stresses conditions; interpretation may change
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./14/rows/3/2: Still unknown; evaluate relative expectations and other forces
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./15/children: Words such as hawkish and dovish are shorthand for an interpretation of relatively restrictive or accommodative policy intentions. They are not numerical probabilities or permanent identities. Attribute the label to the analyst using it and explain which passages support it. A statement can contain mixed messages, and a press conference may clarify or complicate the first reading.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./16/children: A percentage point describes the difference between two percentage rates. One basis point is 0.01 percentage point, so 100 basis points equal one percentage point. A move from 4.00% to 4.25% is an increase of 0.25 percentage point or 25 basis points. It is also a 6.25% proportional increase in the numerical rate because 0.25/4.00 = 0.0625. These expressions answer different questions.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./17/explanation: Here the rates are entered as percentage numbers: (4.25 − 4.00) × 100 = 25 basis points.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./18/title: A small rate change is not a 25% rate
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./18/children/0: A French learner reads “25-basis-point increase” and writes 25%. That would confuse the change with an entirely different rate. Keep the old level, new level and difference on separate lines.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./19/children: A difference between two countries’ rates is also measured in percentage points or basis points when using those units. Do not silently compare a policy rate in one country with a ten-year bond yield in another and call it the same instrument. Record maturity, currency, instrument and observation time.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./20/children: A bond is a debt security with terms for payments and repayment, subject to issuer and product risks. A fixed coupon is a contractual payment feature. The market price can change, and yield measures depend on the price and the yield definition. For an existing fixed-rate bond, a higher required market yield generally corresponds to a lower price, other things equal. That relationship does not remove credit, liquidity or currency risks.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./22/children: This is current yield: annual coupon divided by market price. It is not yield to maturity. Yield to maturity also depends on the timing of payments, redemption amount and other contractual assumptions. The table deliberately omits those details so the price/coupon distinction is clear; it must not be used to value a real bond.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./23/title: The same rental cash at a different purchase price
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./23/children/0: A property offering the same annual rent has a different simple rent-to-purchase-price ratio at two different purchase prices. That ratio is not a complete investment return because repairs, sale value and other costs matter. A coupon-to-price ratio is similarly incomplete.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./24/children: A rising government bond yield can reflect changing policy expectations, inflation compensation, term premium, financing concerns or other forces. It does not prove that overseas investors must buy the currency. Some buyers hedge currency exposure; some may sell the asset. Name the possible channel and alternatives.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./25/children: A nominal return describes the change in money units. An inflation-adjusted, or real, return compares that growth with a relevant price-level change. For a simple one-period calculation, real return = (1 + nominal return)/(1 + inflation) − 1 when both are entered as decimals. Subtracting inflation from the nominal rate is a useful approximation for small rates, not the exact compounding calculation.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./26/explanation: An invented 4% nominal return and 3% inflation give about 0.97% real return before fees and taxes.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./27/title: More cash, only a little more purchasing power
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./27/children/0: An Italian saver ends with €104 instead of €100. If the relevant basket costs €103 instead of €100, the cash balance rose by 4%, but the improvement in purchasing power is about 0.97%. A learner should not describe the full €4 as a 4% improvement in what the money can buy.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./28/children: For forward-looking analysis, expected inflation and realised inflation are different inputs. Actual later inflation can differ from the expectation saved today. A quoted real yield for a market instrument can also use conventions more detailed than this household example. Label whether your calculation is hypothetical, backward-looking or based on expectations.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./29/children: A foreign asset’s return matters in the investor’s home currency. A higher stated foreign yield can be outweighed by an adverse exchange-rate change, fees, taxes, credit loss or hedging costs. A change in relative rates may influence currency demand, but how much was expected and how investments are funded or hedged also matters.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./30/title: Compare savings in euros and yen carefully
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./30/children/0: A German family compares a euro savings offer with a Japanese relative’s yen offer. Before calling one better, they identify the currency of their future bills, account terms, fees, reliability and the exchange rate for converting back. A higher quoted rate in yen or euros is only one input. Borrowing in one currency to buy another adds funding and exchange-rate risks rather than making the difference free income.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./31/title: Interest cannot cancel every exchange-rate loss
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./31/children/0: Use a hypothetical UK saver with £100 converted into a foreign-currency asset. Assume the asset gains 4% in its own currency, and that currency’s value in pounds then falls by 8%. With no fees or taxes, home value is £100 × 1.04 × 0.92 = £95.68. That is a 4.32% loss in pounds despite the positive foreign return.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./32/alt: A £100 teaching investment grows by 4% locally, then an 8% fall in the foreign currency leaves £95.68 in home value.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./32/caption: The invented, unleveraged arithmetic separates asset return from currency return. It does not represent a platform’s financing schedule or a recommended investment.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./33/children: A carry trade typically seeks to benefit from differences in funding and investment returns while accepting other risks. Retail leveraged Forex financing is a product-specific charge or credit, not automatically the simple difference between two central-bank policy rates. Contract terms, spreads, markups, holding days, account conversion and market changes matter. Never use this example as a rollover quote.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./34/children/0: Leverage can amplify currency losses and financing costs. A positive stated rate differential does not ensure a positive total return. Keep the currency, asset, funding and product assumptions visible.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./35/children: Risk-on and risk-off describe broad interpretations of willingness to take risk or preference for protection. They are not official market switches with one universal measurement. Shares, bond prices, volatility, credit conditions and currencies can offer different evidence. Relationships may vary across events and time periods.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./36/title: Different families react differently to uncertainty
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./36/children/0: A household in the United States postpones a large purchase during uncertainty; another household in Japan needs to buy a replacement refrigerator immediately. The same news does not produce an identical action for every household. Market participants also have different obligations, positions and constraints.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./37/children: The US dollar or Japanese yen may be discussed as defensive currencies in some episodes, but that description does not promise their direction in every episode or against every other currency. Funding flows, interest-rate expectations, domestic news and positioning can change the result. A risk label needs dated observations and an alternative explanation.

forex:policy-and-market-relationships./38/rows/2/1: Inflation or financing concern may matter
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./38/rows/2/2: Maturity, expectations and unrelated flows may differ
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./39/children: Correlation observed in one sample is not a law and does not establish causation. Do not use one chart screenshot to prove that an index and a currency always move together. Record the sample, frequency and competing causes before drawing a relationship.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./40/children: Commodity prices can affect countries through export receipts, import costs, business investment and government finances. Australia, Canada, Brazil and South Africa have relevant commodity sectors, but their currencies are not simple copies of one commodity chart. Trade composition, domestic conditions, global demand, policy, hedging and other financial flows also matter.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./41/title: A Canadian exporter’s two moving prices
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./41/children/0: A Canadian business receives US$100 for a shipment in a simplified example. At invented USD/CAD 1.30 the receipt converts to C$130; at 1.25 it converts to C$125 before fees. The foreign sale price and the currency conversion both affect the home receipt. A stronger commodity price alone does not tell you the final home-currency revenue.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./42/children: An importing business can face a different effect from an exporter. For an Indian firm buying energy abroad, higher commodity prices can raise costs while an exchange-rate change adds another influence. A change in crude oil may have different implications for Canada and an importing economy, but the full currency outcome still depends on other forces.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./43/children/0: Avoid “oil up means CAD up” or “gold up means every related currency up” as automatic rules. State the export/import channel, pair, horizon and alternative explanations. A commodity relationship is a hypothesis to examine, not an entry signal.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./44/children: Elections, conflict, sanctions, disasters and changes in trade arrangements can affect activity, confidence, prices and payment channels. Their timing and consequences may be uncertain or unscheduled. Distinguish a verified announcement from a rumour, and an announced proposal from a measure already in force. Use responsible sources and treat people affected by these events with respect.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./45/children/0: A Brazilian shop has a delivery schedule, but a port disruption changes the arrival time and costs. The economic calendar did not contain that disruption as a neatly timed data release. A calendar helps organise scheduled events without covering all risks.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./46/children: Look for the original authority’s statement, a timestamp and independent confirmation where appropriate. A screenshot of a headline may omit a correction, date or important condition. Do not invent a precise price target for an event whose facts are still uncertain. Pausing observation or demo activity can be a complete decision when the information or execution conditions are unclear.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./47/children: Build a two-sided scenario: which observation might support your interpretation, which could weaken it, and which assumptions remain unknown? A narrative about rates or commodities does not replace a cash-risk worksheet or the earlier lesson on combined exposure. Several positions can share the same currency even when their pairs look different.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./48/title: Two different pairs still depend on the dollar
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./48/children/0: A learner holds hypothetical EUR/USD and GBP/USD long positions. Both include being short USD under the conventional pair interpretation. forex:policy-and-market-relationships./49/description: Use supported EUR/USD and GBP/USD separately with the actual stated demo size, USD account and conversion 1. Enter hypothetical adverse exits, then add the losses and charges in the account worksheet. The tool calculates scenarios; it does not predict an event, measure correlation or guarantee an account loss limit.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./50/children: Check pending orders as well as open positions. A headline may arrive while several orders can activate or exits may fill worse than planned. If information, conversion or product terms are missing, keep the position calculation unresolved and record a skip instead of substituting a confident economic story.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./51/prompt: A policy rate changes from 4.00% to 4.25%. Express the change in percentage points and basis points.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./52/children: It increases by 0.25 percentage point, or 25 basis points. The new rate is 4.25%, not 25%.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./53/prompt: A bond pays a fixed annual coupon of 4 units. What are the simplified current yields at prices 100 and 80? Is that yield to maturity?
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./54/children: 4% and 5%. These are annual coupon divided by price, not yield to maturity. A full valuation needs payment timing, redemption and other terms.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./55/prompt: A foreign asset gains 4% while its currency’s home value falls 8%. What happens to an initial home value of 100 before fees?
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./56/children: 100 × 1.04 × 0.92 = 95.68, a loss of 4.32%. Positive asset return does not guarantee positive home-currency return.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./57/prompt: A central bank leaves today’s rate unchanged. Can the announcement still change expectations?
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./58/children: Yes. Its statement, projections or explanation may change expectations about later policy. That still does not guarantee a currency direction. Record the decision and the future-path interpretation separately.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./59/title: Explain it in your own words
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./59/points/0: Distinguish monetary/fiscal decisions, current rates and future-path expectations.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./59/points/1: Calculate basis points and separate bond yield, real return and currency return.
forex:policy-and-market-relationships./59/points/2: Describe conditional risk and commodity relationships without automatic trading rules.

News, policy, calendars and relationships cannot guarantee price direction, execution or a maximum loss. Leverage, costs, conversion, gaps and product terms matter. Keep essential living money outside trading experiments.
